lib_riddler.text: {greeting} The Exeter Book lives here. A thousand years old, given to the cathedral by Bishop Leofric. Poems, wisdom, laments, and riddles.

Some are about an onion, a key or a shield, written so they sound terribly rude. The monks knew exactly what they were doing. Some of the oldest rude jokes in English, and the monks wrote them down on purpose.

then.text: Here's one from the Exeter Book, in modern words. A moth ate words. I thought it a strange thing, that a worm should swallow the song of a man, a thief in the dark, and be no wiser for it.
A bookworm! A moth grub eating the vellum. It ate the words and learned nothing. We've all had students like that.

else.text: Here, a prize. Scones. Don't eat them in the library.
Not quite. It's a bookworm: a moth's grub, chewing the vellum. All those words inside it, and none the wiser.
Another time. The book's waited a thousand years, it can wait till Tuesday.
